    Week plans

    Five dinners, one shop

    Five easy weeknight dinners from the book, each on the table within an hour of getting home (most well under), picked so they share ingredients (a bunch of spring onions or a tray of chicken thighs goes across several nights) while every night is different. Add a plan and the shopping list combines it all.

    Cooking for
    Prices

    Leave out

    Allergies, dietary needs or just not a fan: plans and picks skip any dinner with these.

      Matched on ingredient names in the book, so always check the labels on jars and packets.

      Build your own

      Pick up to four dinners you're craving. The rest of the week is filled in with easy dinners that share their shopping.

        Savings are estimates from typical supermarket pack prices, checked 16 Nov 2026 and rising with food inflation since. They compare buying once with buying for each dinner on its own, and count what you've ticked as already in your kitchen on What can I cook?

        Basics

        Supermarket shortcuts for the nights you don't want to cook from scratch. They turn up in the plans above too.

        • Butter ChickenA jar of sauce, a tray of chicken thighs and a pack of naan: a takeaway night from the supermarket.
        • Dumpling NightA bag of frozen dumplings, pan-fried until the bottoms crackle, with bok choy and plenty of chilli crisp.
        • Fish and ChipsFriday fish and chips without the queue: crumbed fish and oven chips from the freezer, with peas and lemon.
        • Hot Chook and ColeslawA hot chicken from the deli counter, a bag of coleslaw and soft rolls: dinner on the table before the chicken's cooled.
        • LaksaA jar of laksa paste, coconut milk and chicken: a big, spicy bowl of soup from the international aisle.
        • Old El Paso TacosTaco night from the kit: everyone builds their own, and the table ends up covered in lettuce.
        • Pies and PeasA meat pie from the freezer with peas and a good squirt of tomato sauce: the footy classic, at the kitchen table.
        • Pizza NightTwo frozen pizzas and a bag of salad: no one has to cook, and everyone gets their favourite slice.
        • Ravioli and SauceFresh ravioli and a tub of sauce from the fridge section: dinner in the time it takes the water to boil.
        • Schnitty and ChipsCrumbed chicken schnitzels from the meat section, oven chips and a salad: the pub favourite without leaving home.
        • Snags in BreadThe sausage sizzle at home: snags and soft onions folded into a slice of white bread with plenty of tomato sauce.
